validated_work_order.understanding: A custom report's conditions button is icon-only: CompactFiltersButton renders a bare Button whose only child is SvgFilter, with no text node and no aria-label, so its accessible name is empty. The e2e page model works around that by enumerating every button in the report page, skipping any that carries an aria-label or non-empty text, and clicking the first whose bounding box sits right of x=850 (custom-report-page.ts:55-77). That is the only way the suite reaches the conditions menu. It is also actively fragile, not merely untidy: the scan skips every named button, so the moment the toolbar gains any named button it silently selects a different control. The fix is to give the button a name and locate it by that name, which also retires the geometry. The second half of the ticket is the e2e file's own duplication - selectOnlyBillsGroup and switchToAnyOf each exist twice, byte-identical apart from a comment, so hoisting them is what makes the first change cheap. This is the fourth planning pass; the single objection from the third rejection is answered in AC-6, out_of_scope[0] and debate_summary below.
validated_work_order.root_cause: The control has no accessible name, and the locator that had to compensate for that compensates with geometry. The x>850 threshold is a function of the fixed-width content to the button's left, not of viewport width: ReportTopbar renders nine GraphButtons, three 1px dividers and a SnapshotButton, all flexShrink: 0, then a SpaceBetween with flex:1, flexWrap:'nowrap' and justifyContent:'space-between' (ReportTopbar.tsx:227-233) whose first child is the compact FilterButton. Inside a space-between row the first child sits at the region's left edge, so narrowing the window pushes SaveReport right rather than moving the filter button left. What does follow from the code is that 850 is a fragile sum of sidebar widths (ReportSidebar minWidth 225, SidebarShell MIN_SIDEBAR_WIDTH 200) with little slack, and that a control with no name cannot be addressed at all except by such a sum.
validated_work_order.approach: Add aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing bare Button in CompactFiltersButton, reusing the translation key the sibling tooltip on this very control already uses (FiltersMenu.tsx:744) and matching the pattern every other icon-only control in the topbar uses (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:42-43). An aria-label adds no rendered node, so no VRT snapshot moves. Then reduce openConditionsMenu to a single getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click(), which deletes the button scan, the hasName probe, the boundingBox call, the x>850 comparison and the now-unreachable throw, and hoist the two duplicated e2e helpers to the body of the 'custom reports' describe. Because no CI-executed check touches packages/desktop-client/e2e/ (.sdlc/config.yml:172 e2e is empty; vite.config.mts:406 vitest includes only src/**; desktop-client tsconfig.json:33 excludes e2e), the e2e suite is not a gate and is treated throughout as a local-only run in qa_script; the CI-executed backing for the accessible name is a new unit test under src/, and the page-model and suite criteria are stated as structural properties checkable by reading, never as a suite nobody runs.

files.change: Import useTranslation from 'react-i18next' (after the existing `import React from 'react';`, matching FiltersMenu.tsx:6), call `const { t } = useTranslation();` at the top of CompactFiltersButton, and pass aria-label={t('Filters')} to the existing `<Button variant="bare" onPress={onPress} style={{ minWidth: 20 }}>`. Nothing else changes: the SvgFilter child and its width/height/flexShrink, the minWidth, the bare variant and the onPress plumbing stay exactly as they are, and no text node is introduced.
files.why: This is the root of the ticket. 'Filters' is already a translation key in this feature - the tooltip content on this same control at FiltersMenu.tsx:744 - so no new string enters the catalog and generate:i18n output is unaffected. aria-label rather than a visually-hidden span or a title attribute, because aria-label is the pattern the neighbouring icon-only toolbar buttons already use and it adds no DOM node, hence no layout shift and no VRT movement. The component library Button spreads restProps onto the underlying react-aria Button (component-library/src/Button.tsx:136,169), and aria-label already reaches the DOM through that path in GraphButton and SnapshotButton, so no plumbing is needed.

files.change: Replace the entire body of openConditionsMenu with one statement: `await this.pageContent.getByRole('button', { name: 'Filters', exact: true }).click();`. Delete the buttons/count loop, the hasName probe, the boundingBox() call, the box.x > 850 comparison and the unreachable throw at the end of the method. Rewrite the JSDoc at :50-54 to say the button is addressed by its accessible name rather than by its position among the topbar buttons. Keep the method name, the no-arg signature and the this.pageContent receiver - reports.test.ts calls it at :291 and :458 and this is its only definition.
files.why: Once the control has a name, the geometric scan is not just fragile but actively harmful: it skips every named button, so it would silently pick a different control the moment the toolbar gains any named button. exact:true keeps the compact and non-compact variants distinguishable - the accounts page's sibling is named 'Filter' (FiltersButton.tsx:13, used at account-page.ts:56) and Playwright's default name matching is substring-based, so an inexact 'Filters' would match that button too.

files.why: The duplication is what made openConditionsMenu's two callers expensive to fix - each one carried private copies of the two helpers, so the same edit had to be reasoned about in two places. The new test exists because IAC-6 asks for the suite to hold at a narrower width, and it is described as what it is: a positive assertion that the role-and-name locator resolves at 1024px. It is green before and after this change and is not claimed as a regression test for the old scan. The finally that restores the viewport is defensive tidiness so the test is self-contained, NOT protection against cross-test leakage: the outer beforeEach at :23-24 opens a fresh page with browser.newPage() and afterEach at :35-37 closes it, and playwright.config.ts `use:` (:16-24) sets no viewport key, so every test starts at Playwright's default 1280x720 - which is also why the pre-existing :177, set to 1280x700 unrestored and outside any try, does no harm to the toMatchThemeScreenshots cases at :667 and :675 that run after it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give the button a visually hidden text node instead of an aria-label (a <Text> with a screen-reader-only style).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It adds a DOM node to a bare button with an explicit minWidth: 20, which is the kind of thing that moves pixels and invalidates visual-regression snapshots for no accessibility gain over aria-label. aria-label is what the neighbouring GraphButton and SnapshotButton already do.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the positional scan but widen or recompute the threshold, or scan for the button next to a known landmark.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the control without an accessible name, which is the actual defect: the button is announced to a screen reader as just "button". Fixing the locator instead of the name treats the symptom. It also leaves the scan's skip-named-buttons logic in place, which would silently pick a different control as soon as the toolbar gains one.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a data-testid to CompactFiltersButton and point the page model at it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves the accessible name empty. The repo's convention for icon-only toolbar controls is aria-label (GraphButton.tsx:42, SnapshotButton.tsx:42-43), and there are already established name-based e2e locators (account-page.ts:56). The ticket explicitly prefers a hook a person benefits from, and permits a test id only if no name can be given - a name can.

alternatives_considered.approach: Also wrap the pre-existing setViewportSize at reports.test.ts:177 in a try/finally while the file is being edited.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is unrelated to the ticket and would make AC-6 assert something this change does not control. The objection that forced the AC-6 rewrite was precisely that the old criterion claimed a file-wide property the diff did not establish; repeating that in a different form would be the same error. Leaving :177 untouched and describing the viewport shape instead of counting hits is the honest version.

Asserting the shape - the new case owns both of its viewport calls, and :177 is untouched - stays true as line numbers move and needs no arithmetic.
